mainTopic: עדים זוממין: splitting punishments, what counts as הזמה, and how the timing of the sentence matters
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: רבי מאיר learns הכרזה, the public announcement when עדים זוממין are punished, from the words ישמעו ויראו. A new משנה teaches that עדים זוממין split a money penalty but each one gets the full מלקות. אביי learns this from the word רשע, which links lashes to the death penalty, and רבא learns it from כאשר זמם. Next, another משנה rules that witnesses become זוממין only when the second group says 'you were with us,' not when they just contradict the event. רבי יהודה disagrees about one group making many groups זוממין. The גמרא finds the source for this rule in עד שקר and in סרה. רבא then gives cases showing that an alibi works only if the first testimony was truly impossible: we assume normal eyesight and normal travel speed. Finally, רבא teaches that זוממין are punished only if the accused had not yet been sentenced when they testified, for death penalties and for fines alike. The amud ends by quoting רבי יהודה's word איסטטית, and the discussion of it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse is needed for the public announcement
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: according to the view being defended, a verse is needed for הכרזה, a public announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: [That verse is needed] for the public announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the earlier discussion. It says that a certain verse is used to teach הכרזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When witnesses are punished, the court publicly announces why, so that others will learn not to do the same. This one word closes the earlier answer and sets up the next question about רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A public announcement of a person's sin when the court punishes him, so others will be afraid to do the same

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the verse a different job, so it cannot be used for the other teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse in question teaches הכרזה.

steps.title: Where רבי מאיר learns the public announcement from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר gets הכרזה, and answers that he learns it from the words ישמעו ויראו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, where does he learn the announcement from? He learns the announcement from 'they will hear and fear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: what does רבי מאיר do about הכרזה? It answers that he learns it from a different phrase in the פסוק, ישמעו ויראו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר gets הכרזה from the words ישמעו ויראו, the other words of the same פסוק are free for him to use for a different teaching. This is a common move: two opinions agree on a law but get it from different words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They will hear and fear,' a phrase from the פסוק about punishing עדים זוממין (דברים 19:20)
'It comes out from,' meaning this law is learned from this source

phrases.notes: He's asking: if רבי מאיר uses that verse for something else, where does he get the announcement from?

phrases.english: He derives the announcement from 'they will hear and fear.'
phrases.notes: דברים 19:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי מאיר handles the law of הכרזה that the other view learned from the verse in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns it from ישמעו ויראו.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views require הכרזה. They only disagree about which words in the פסוק teach it.

steps.title: Money is split, lashes are not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that עדים זוממין split a money penalty between them, but they do not split a penalty of מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We divide a money penalty among the witnesses, but we do not divide lashes among them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a short rule about how עדים זוממין are punished as a group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים זוממין get the same punishment they tried to bring on the person they testified against. The משנה says that if that punishment is money, the witnesses share it. If it is lashes, they do not share it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
'We split into thirds,' meaning we divide the penalty among the witnesses, however many there are
Lashes, the punishment of מלקות

steps.confusionAlert: מְשַׁלְּשִׁין sounds like 'into three,' but it applies even to two witnesses. It means each witness pays only a share of the total.

phrases.english: but we do not divide [the penalty] in lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין split a money penalty but not a lashes penalty.

steps.title: The משנה gives examples of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה illustrates: false testimony about a 200 זוז debt is split among the witnesses, but false testimony that he deserves forty lashes makes each witness get forty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If they testified that he owes his friend two hundred זוז and they were found to be זוממין, they split it among themselves. But if they testified that he deserves forty lashes and they were found to be זוממין, each one gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its rule with two examples: one about money and one about lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the money case, together the witnesses pay the full 200 זוז, each paying a share. In the lashes case, each witness gets the full number of lashes on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin
Witnesses proven false because other witnesses say they were somewhere else at the time
'Forty lashes,' the תורה's term for the punishment of מלקות

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forty lashes' is the תורה's wording, but in practice the punishment is thirty-nine lashes.
steps.whatToRemember: Money: the witnesses split it and pay one full total together. Lashes: each witness gets the full amount.

phrases.aramaic: הֶעִידוּהוּ שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לַחֲבֵירוֹ מָאתַיִם זוּז
phrases.english: If they testified about him that he owes his fellow two hundred zuz
and they were found to be conspiring witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הֶעִידוּהוּ שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב מַלְקוֹת אַרְבָּעִים
phrases.english: But if they testified about him that he is liable to forty lashes
and they were found to be conspiring witnesses,
each and every one receives forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples for the rule in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For 200 זוז the witnesses divide the payment; for forty lashes each witness gets forty.

steps.title: What is the source for not splitting lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's rule. It is setting up the answers of אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main question is why lashes are not divided the way money is. The next steps give two different sources.

keyTerms.meaning: The תלמוד's discussion of the משנה
'From where are these things?' A request for the source in the פסוקים

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that lashes are not divided among עדים זוממין.

steps.title: אביי: lashes are like the death penalty, which cannot be done halfway
steps.stepSummary: אביי compares מלקות to מיתת בית דין through the shared word רשע. Just as there is no half death, there are no half lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Wicked' is said about people who deserve lashes, and 'wicked' is said about people who deserve death by the court. Just as there, there is no half death, so too here, there are no half lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by linking two פסוקים that both use the word רשע. One is about lashes and one is about the court's death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot give a person half a death, so a death penalty can never be split among witnesses. Since the same word links lashes to death, lashes also cannot be split. So each witness gets the full lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Wicked,' the word used both for those who get lashes (דברים 25:2) and for those who get the death penalty (במדבר 35:31)
Death penalties given by the court
In half, partially
'Just as there, so too here,' the formula for applying a law from one case to another

phrases.english: 'Wicked' is stated regarding those liable to lashes,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2

phrases.english: and 'wicked' is stated regarding those liable to court-imposed death.
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:31

phrases.english: Just as there, there is no half death,
so too here, there are no half lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word רשע links lashes to the death penalty, which cannot be divided.

steps.title: רבא: each witness must receive what he planned to do
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source: the פסוק requires כאשר זמם לעשות לאחיו, and splitting the lashes would not do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We need 'as he planned to do to his brother,' and that would not happen [if the lashes were split].
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the same question. He uses the main פסוק about עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each witness tried to have the man get the full lashes. If a witness got only part of the lashes, he would not get what he planned to do to his brother. So each must get the full lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As he planned to do to his brother' (דברים 19:19), the source for punishing עדים זוממין
'We need,' meaning this is a requirement
'And it is not there,' meaning the requirement would not be met

phrases.english: We need 'as he conspired to do to his brother,'
phrases.notes: דברים 19:19

phrases.english: and it would not be fulfilled.
phrases.notes: He means: if each witness got only part of the lashes, he would not get what he planned for the other man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Splitting lashes would not fulfill כאשר זמם.

steps.title: Then money should not be split either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: by his logic, each witness should pay the whole sum too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, money too [should not be split]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reasoning by applying it to money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each witness also planned to make the man lose the full 200 זוז. So by רבא's logic, each one should pay 200 זוז, yet the משנה says they split it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so,' an opening for a challenge that follows from the last statement
Also, too

phrases.notes: Meaning: then each witness should pay the full sum, since that is what each one planned to cause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning should make each witness pay the full money too, which goes against the משנה.

steps.title: Money adds up, lashes do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that payments can be added together, but lashes cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money combines; lashes do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It explains why money and lashes are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the witnesses each pay a share, the man still receives the full 200 זוז, so כאשר זמם is fulfilled by all of them together. Lashes on different bodies cannot be added together into one full punishment, so each witness must get them all.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines, adds up together

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, lashes are like death and cannot be done halfway. According to רבא, כאשר זמם requires the full punishment. Money is split because the shares add up to the full amount, but lashes cannot be added together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה treats money and lashes differently. It also clarifies what כאשר זמם requires: the full planned harm must be returned, whether all together or by each witness alone.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference between money and lashes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought כאשר זמם requires each witness to pay the full sum.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shares of money add up to the full loss, so כאשר זמם is fulfilled; lashes cannot be added up, so each witness gets all of them.

steps.title: The new rule: witnesses must be attacked personally
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that witnesses only become זוממין when the second group impeaches the witnesses themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses are not considered זוממין until the second group impeaches the witnesses themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a general rule about when witnesses count as עדים זוממין. The next line will explain it with an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every attack on testimony turns witnesses into זוממין. The second group has to say something about the first witnesses personally, not just about the event they described.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting false witnesses who receive the punishment they tried to cause
That they impeach the witnesses themselves

phrases.english: Witnesses are not made into conspiring witnesses

phrases.notes: The second group must speak about the first witnesses' own whereabouts, not only about the event.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הָעֵדִים נַעֲשִׂים זוֹמְמִין עַד שֶׁיָּזֵימּוּ אֶת עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion about lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses become זוממין only when the witnesses themselves are impeached.

steps.title: Example: arguing about the event is not הזמה
steps.stepSummary: If the second group says the victim or the killer was with them elsewhere, the first witnesses are not זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Witnesses said, 'We testify that so-and-so killed a person.' Others said to them, 'How can you testify this? The victim, or the killer, was with us that day in another place!' These first witnesses are not זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the first half of its example. Here the second group attacks the story, not the witnesses, so it is not הזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the victim or the killer was with us' contradicts what the first witnesses described. It says nothing about where the first witnesses themselves were, so it does not meet the rule from the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an example)
A plain contradiction of the testimony, which is not the same as הזמה
So-and-so, a certain person

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not זוממין' only means these witnesses do not get the punishment of עדים זוממין. It does not mean their testimony wins.

phrases.english: Others said to them: "How can you testify?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי נֶהֱרָג זֶה אוֹ הַהוֹרֵג זֶה
phrases.english: For this one who was killed, or this killer,

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה עִמָּנוּ אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי!״
phrases.english: was with us that day in such-and-such a place!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first case explaining the rule of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attacking the event, about the victim or the killer, does not make the witnesses זוממין.

steps.title: Example: 'You were with us' is הזמה
steps.stepSummary: If the second group says the first witnesses themselves were with them elsewhere, the first witnesses are זוממין and are executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they said, 'How can you testify? You were with us that day in another place!', these are זוממין and are executed based on the second group's word.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second half of the example. Now the attack is on the witnesses themselves, so they are זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'you were with us' prove the first witnesses could not have seen the event at all. This fits the rule of step 10 exactly, so they receive the death penalty they tried to cause.

keyTerms.meaning: You were with us, the classic wording of הזמה
They are executed
On their word, meaning on the second group's testimony

steps.whatToRemember: Contradicting the story ('the victim was with us') is not הזמה. Placing the witnesses elsewhere ('you were with us') is הזמה.

phrases.english: But if they said to them: "How can you testify?
that day in such-and-such a place!"
and they are executed on their word.
phrases.notes: "Their word" means the testimony of the second group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 11 by giving the case that does count as הזמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'you were with us elsewhere' makes the witnesses זוממין, and they are executed.

steps.title: Even a hundred groups made זוממין are all executed
steps.stepSummary: If more groups come and the same second group makes each of them זוממין, every group is executed, even a hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: If others came and were made זוממין, and yet others came and were made זוממין, even a hundred groups, all of them are executed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case where many groups testify and are all made זוממין by the same second group. This is the first opinion, and רבי יהודה will disagree next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new group backs up the first testimony, and the same second group says each one was with them elsewhere. The first opinion treats every group as real עדים זוממין, no matter how many there are.

keyTerms.meaning: Other witnesses, meaning another group
And they made them זוממין
All of them are executed

phrases.english: If others came, and they made them conspiring witnesses,
phrases.notes: A new group backs up the first testimony, and the second group says this group was also with them.

phrases.english: and others came, and they made them conspiring witnesses,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the הזמה case of step 12 to many groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any number of groups made זוממין by one group are all executed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: this looks like a plot, so only the first group dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה calls this a conspiracy and rules that only the first group is executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: This is a conspiracy, and only the first group alone is executed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one group keeps making every new group זוממין, רבי יהודה becomes suspicious of that second group. He limits the death penalty to the first group only.

keyTerms.meaning: A conspiracy, a plotting gang
The first group of witnesses

phrases.notes: He means the second group looks like a gang set on knocking down anyone who testifies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the first group is executed, because the repeated הזמה is suspicious.

steps.title: Where do we learn the משנה's opening rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that witnesses become זוממין only when they themselves are impeached.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the opening rule of the משנה. This sets up רב אדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the rule in steps 10 to 12: why only 'you were with us' counts as הזמה. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: This is asking about the opening rule: only 'you were with us' makes witnesses זוממין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening rule of the משנה and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that הזמה requires impeaching the witnesses themselves.

steps.title: רב אדא: the testimony's 'body' must be proven false
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא learns from the words עד שקר that the witnesses themselves must be shown false.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said: The פסוק says, 'And behold, a false witness; the witness testified falsely.' This means the body of the testimony, the witnesses themselves, must be proven false.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא answers the question of step 15 with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the witness himself 'false,' not only his words. So the falseness must reach the witnesses personally by showing they were somewhere else. Arguing only about the event is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse
A false witness
The body of the testimony, meaning the witnesses themselves

steps.whatToRemember: הזמה must prove the witnesses themselves false, and this is learned from עד שקר in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Adda said: As the verse says:
"And behold, the witness is a false witness;

phrases.notes: דברים 19:18

phrases.english: until the body of the testimony is proven false.
phrases.notes: The 'body' is the witnesses themselves. They are shown not to have been there at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'והנה עד שקר העד שקר ענה' teaches that the witnesses themselves must be proven false.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל gives another source: the testimony itself must be false
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל learn from the word סרה that witnesses become זוממין only when the גוף of the testimony, meaning the witnesses themselves, is shown false.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "To testify perversely (סרה) against him." This means the witnesses are not זוממין until the main body of the testimony is made false.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question in Step 15. It brings another source for the rule that the testimony itself must be shown false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא learned the rule from עד שקר, and the school of רבי ישמעאל learns the same rule from the word סרה, reading it as the גוף of the testimony "turning aside." As in step 16, the גוף of the testimony means the witnesses themselves. Contradicting the event ("the killer was with us") is not enough; the witnesses must be shown not to have been there.

keyTerms.meaning: Perverse or false; related to the root "to turn aside"
To testify or answer
The body, or core, of the testimony

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.notes: דברים 19:16

phrases.english: until the body of the testimony is made false.
phrases.notes: The word תסרה comes from the same root as סרה in the פסוק. That shared root is the source of the lesson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source alongside רב אדא's answer to the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that witnesses are only זוממין when they themselves, and the core of their testimony, are shown false?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the word סרה: the testimony must be false at its core.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the same rule: עד שקר (רב אדא) and סרה (school of רבי ישמעאל). Both teach that the testimony itself must be shown false.

steps.title: East or west of the building: can they see from there?
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the second witnesses place the first witnesses on the other side of a building, we check whether one could see across. If one could, there is no הזמה. If not, the first witnesses are זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two witnesses came and said, "So-and-so killed a person on the east side of the building." Then two others came and said, "But you were with us on the west side of the building!" We look into it. If people standing on the west side can see the east side, the first witnesses are not זוממין. If not, they are זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a practical case of an alibi. The second witnesses place the first witnesses close to the murder scene, just on the other side of a building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second witnesses do not say the first witnesses were far away. They only say they were on the other side of the בירה. So the alibi works only if the first witnesses truly could not have seen the event from where they stood. The court checks what is physically possible from that spot.

keyTerms.meaning: A large building or fortress
Witnesses proven false by an alibi; they receive the punishment they tried to bring on the accused
We look into it, we check
So-and-so

phrases.english: "On the east side of the building
"But weren't you with us on the west side of the building!"
if, when people stand on the west side of the building,
they can see to the east side of the building,
and if not, these are זוממין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of הזמה to how it works in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An alibi works only if the first witnesses truly could not have seen the event from where the second witnesses place them.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say the building case, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: his ruling seems so obvious that there was no need to say it. This sets up the next step, which explains what the ruling adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course, if the witnesses could see the event, they are not liars. The גמרא assumes every teaching should add something new, so it asks what רבא is teaching here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why did this need to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's ruling in Step 18 adds anything.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is plain that people who could see the event are not false, the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We do not worry about unusually sharp eyesight
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that we judge by normal eyesight. If a normal person could not see across, we do not suggest that these witnesses had extra-sharp vision.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: Let us be concerned that these witnesses have very sharp eyesight. So רבא teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the new point in רבא's ruling: the court goes by what a normal person can see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is in the second half of the ruling. When a normal person cannot see across, the witnesses are זוממין. We might have thought they get off because they might have unusually strong vision. רבא teaches that we do not take that possibility into account.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought, and you would have been wrong
Let us be concerned about it
Strong or sharp eyesight (literally "healthy light")
So it teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: let us be concerned about sharp eyesight;
so he teaches us that we do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by identifying the new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows what the ruling adds (מהו דתימא ... קמשמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps these witnesses had extra-sharp vision, so they should not be made זוממין.
steps.terutzMaskana: We go by normal eyesight. If a normal person could not see across, they are זוממין.
steps.confusionAlert: The new point is not that people who could see are telling the truth. That part really is obvious. The new point is that we ignore the chance of unusually sharp eyesight.

steps.title: סורא in the morning, נהרדעא in the evening: could they travel in time?
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the alibi places the first witnesses in another city later that day, we check whether the trip could be made in that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Two witnesses came and said, "So-and-so killed a person in סורא on Sunday morning." Then two others came and said, "On Sunday evening you were with us in נהרדעא!" We look into it. If one can travel from סורא to נהרדעא between morning and evening, they are not זוממין. If not, they are זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second alibi case. This time the gap is in time and distance instead of a building blocking the view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two testimonies are about different times of the same day, so they do not clash directly. The first witnesses could have seen the murder in the morning and then traveled. They are proven false only if the trip from סורא to נהרדעא cannot be made between morning and evening.

keyTerms.meaning: Morning
Evening
The first day of the week, Sunday
One is able to travel

phrases.english: "In Sura, in the morning, on Sunday,
you were with us in Nehardea!"
one can travel from Sura to Nehardea,
and if not, they are זוממין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical case from רבא. It applies the same test, whether the first testimony was physically possible, to time and distance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An alibi at a later time in a distant place works only if the trip could not have been made in that time.
steps.whatToRemember: In both of רבא's cases, an alibi creates הזמה only if it makes the first testimony truly impossible: they could not see it, or they could not have gotten there in time.

steps.title: Isn't the travel-time ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling about checking whether the witnesses could have reached the other city in time, calling it obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say his city-travel ruling from Step 21, since it seems obvious. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trip could not be made in the time available, it seems obvious that the alibi holds and the first witnesses are זוממין. The גמרא wants to know what new idea רבא is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.notes: This is about רבא's last ruling: checking whether the witnesses could get from one city to the other in time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבא's ruling in Step 21, just as Step 19 challenged the building ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that we check whether the trip to the other city could be made in the time available.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems to state plain common sense, so it should not need to be taught.

steps.title: No worrying about a flying camel
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that we judge by normal travel speed and do not imagine an unusually fast camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should worry that they rode a 'flying camel' that could cover the distance super fast. So רבא teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא's ruling rules out a far-fetched possibility: that the witnesses traveled on an extremely fast camel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רבא's ruling, one might think the first witnesses could defend themselves by saying they had some unusually fast way to travel. רבא teaches that we judge by normal travel times, just as Step 20 judged by normal eyesight.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (this introduces the mistaken idea)
A 'flying camel,' meaning an extremely fast camel
He teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: In הזמה, we judge by normal human ability: normal eyesight (Step 20) and normal travel speed (this step).

phrases.notes: This means 'You might have thought...'. It sets up the mistake that רבא comes to rule out.

phrases.english: Let us be concerned about a flying camel,
so he teaches us that we are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מהו דתימא ליחוש לגמלא פרחא קא משמע לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden possibility (a mistaken thought) that the ruling rules out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps we should consider that the witnesses used an unusually fast camel, so their story could still be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: We go by normal travel speed. Unusual possibilities like a flying camel are ignored.

steps.title: The murder happened on a different day: the first witnesses are still killed
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the alibi witnesses say the accused did kill, but on a different day, the first witnesses are still punished as זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: Two witnesses came and said, 'On Sunday so-and-so killed a person.' Then two others came and said, 'You were with us on Sunday, but it was on Monday that so-and-so killed that person.' And even if they said, 'On Friday so-and-so killed the person,' the first witnesses are killed. This is because when they testified, the man was not yet sentenced to death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling. The first witnesses are proven זוממין through an alibi, even though the second witnesses agree that the accused really is a killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the first witnesses did no harm, since the man really did kill. But רבא says what matters is the man's legal status when they testified: he had not yet been sentenced by a court, so they tried to cause the death of a man who was not yet condemned. That makes them liable as זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first day of the week (Sunday)
On the second day of the week (Monday)
Friday
At the time that they testify
Someone already condemned to death

steps.confusionAlert: The second witnesses do not clear the accused. They agree he killed, just on a different day. The first witnesses are still punished, because the man was not yet sentenced when they testified.

phrases.english: and two others came and said

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּתְרֵי בְּשַׁבְּתָא הָרַג פְּלוֹנִי אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ״.
phrases.english: but on Monday so-and-so killed the person."
And not only that, but even if they said

phrases.notes: 'They' means the first pair of witnesses, the ones proven to be זוממין.

phrases.english: because at the time that they testified,
the man was not yet condemned to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר רבא באו שנים ואמרו בחד בשבתא הרג פלוני את הנפש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling from רבא about הזמה, with a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זוממין are executed even if the accused really did kill on another day, as long as he had not been sentenced at the time of their testimony.

steps.title: A משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבא adds, since a משנה already says that זוממין are killed together with the guilty accused.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in a משנה: Therefore, if one of the sets of witnesses is found to be זוממין, he and they are executed, and the second set is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling by pointing to a משנה that seems to teach the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, two sets of witnesses testify against one man. When one set is proven זוממין, the man is still executed based on the other set, and the זוממין are executed too. So the משנה already shows that זוממין are killed even when the accused really is guilty, which is exactly רבא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What is new here?)
A set of witnesses proven to be זוממין
He (the accused) and they (the זוממין) are executed
Exempt from punishment

phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in the מסכת, about two sets of witnesses against one man.

phrases.english: Therefore, if one of them is found to be conspiring –
and the second set is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's ruling in Step 24 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that זוממין are executed even though the accused really killed on another day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already shows that זוממין are killed even when the accused is truly guilty and executed, so רבא's ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The new point: testimony after the verdict
steps.stepSummary: רבא's real point is the second half: if the man had already been sentenced when the witnesses testified, the זוממין are not executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second half, 'which is not the case with a verdict,' is what he needed to teach. Two witnesses came and said, 'On Sunday so-and-so was sentenced to death.' Then two others came and said, 'On Sunday you were with us, but so-and-so was sentenced on Friday.' And even if they said, 'He was sentenced on Monday,' the first witnesses are not executed, because when they testified, the man was already condemned to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא said the first case only to set up the second case, which really is new. In the second case the זוממין are not killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the first witnesses testified only that a court had already sentenced the man. Even though they are proven זוממין about the day, the man was already condemned by the time they testified, so they did not harm someone who was still free of a death sentence. Both halves depend on the same test: the man's status at the moment of testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part (of the teaching)
The final verdict of the court
He needed it (it was necessary to teach)
His sentence was finalized

steps.whatToRemember: The key test is the man's status when the witnesses testify. If he was not yet sentenced, the זוממין are killed. If he was already sentenced, they are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear time-based rule for הזמה: the punishment of זוממין depends on whether their testimony could still have changed the man's fate.

phrases.english: The latter clause, "which is not so with a verdict,"
is what he needed to teach:
phrases.notes: The first case was said only as a lead-in to this second, new case.

phrases.english: and two others came and said

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי״.
phrases.english: but on Friday so-and-so's sentence was finalized."
phrases.notes: Here Friday means the Friday before, so the sentence came even earlier.

phrases.english: And not only that, but even if they said
Because at the time that they testified,
the man was already condemned to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: סיפא מה שאין כן בגמר דין איצטריכא ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by moving the new point of רבא's teaching to its second half.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the new point to the latter clause; the first clause was said only as a lead-in.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling seemed to repeat the משנה about זוממין being executed alongside a guilty accused.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's new point is that if the man was already sentenced when the witnesses testified, the זוממין are not executed.

steps.title: The same rule applies to a fine: witnesses pay if the thief was not yet sentenced
steps.stepSummary: Two witnesses say a man stole and then slaughtered or sold an animal on Sunday. Other witnesses prove the first pair were elsewhere and say the theft was on another day, even an earlier day. The first witnesses still pay, because when they testified the man was not yet obligated to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true for paying a fine. Two witnesses come and say: "On Sunday he stole, then slaughtered or sold the animal." Two more come and say: "On Sunday you were with us. He stole and slaughtered or sold it on Monday." The first witnesses pay. Even if the second pair says he did it on Friday, the first witnesses still pay. This is because at the time they testified, the man was not yet obligated to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רבא's rule about death-penalty cases (steps 24-26) and applies it to a money fine. Here the first witnesses do pay, because the accused had not yet been sentenced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief who slaughters or sells the stolen animal pays a קנס of four or five times its value. The alibi witnesses agree he really did steal, just not on the day the first pair said. Even so, the first pair tried to make him pay through false testimony while he was not yet obligated, so they pay the fine themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Payments of a fine: a set penalty beyond the real damage, here four or five times the animal's value
He stole and then slaughtered or sold the animal, which makes him owe the four- or five-times fine
On Sunday / on Monday (literally 'on day one / day two of the week')
Friday, the day before שבת. Here it is earlier than the first witnesses' Sunday
Someone already obligated to pay, meaning the court has already ruled against him
And not only that, but even: it introduces a bigger case with the same ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the first witnesses go free just because the man really did steal. What matters is that he was not yet sentenced when they testified, so their lie was trying to create a payment he did not yet owe.

phrases.english: And likewise with regard to payments of a fine:
"On Sunday he stole and slaughtered or sold [the animal],"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37. This brings a fine of four or five times the animal's value.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּתְרֵי בְּשַׁבְּתָא גָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר״ –
phrases.english: but on Monday he stole and slaughtered or sold" –

phrases.notes: "They" means the first pair of witnesses, the ones proven false.

phrases.english: And not only that, but even if they said:
"On Friday he stole and slaughtered or sold" –
phrases.notes: This is the Friday before that Sunday, so the theft happened even earlier than the first witnesses claimed.

phrases.english: because at the time they were testifying,
the man was not [yet] obligated to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's death-penalty rule from step 26 into the area of monetary fines, starting with the case where the witnesses pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the accused was not yet sentenced when the first witnesses testified, those witnesses pay the fine once they are proven זוממין, even if he really did steal on a different day, earlier or later.

steps.title: No payment when the thief had already been sentenced before they testified
steps.stepSummary: This time the first witnesses testify that the man stole and was already sentenced. The alibi witnesses show he was in fact already sentenced, on Friday or even on Monday. The first witnesses do not pay, because when they testified the man already owed the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two witnesses come and say: "On Sunday he stole, slaughtered or sold, and was sentenced." Two more come and say: "On Sunday you were with us. He stole, slaughtered or sold, and was sentenced on Friday." Even if the second pair says: "He stole on Sunday and was sentenced on Monday," the first witnesses do not pay. This is because at the time they testified, the man was already obligated to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite case, which matches the second half of רבא's rule from step 26. If the man was already sentenced when the first witnesses testified, they do not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדים זוממין are punished with what they tried to do to the accused. Here their testimony could not create a new obligation, because the court had already made him owe the fine. So there is nothing to pay back, and they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: His case was decided: the court already sentenced him
They do not pay
At the time that they were testifying: the moment that decides the ruling

steps.whatToRemember: For both death and fines, the key question is the timing of the testimony. If the accused was not yet sentenced, the false witnesses are punished. If he was already sentenced, they are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא's rule is a general principle about הזמה. It is not something special to capital cases.

phrases.english: "On Sunday he stole and slaughtered or sold

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת גָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר
phrases.english: but on Friday he stole and slaughtered or sold
and not only that, but even if they said:
"On Sunday he stole and slaughtered or sold,
and on Monday his sentence was decided" –
because at the time they were testifying,
the man was [already] obligated to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאוּ שְׁנַיִם וְאָמְרוּ בְּחַד בְּשַׁבְּתָא גָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר וְנִגְמַר דִּינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case to step 27. Once the sentence came before the testimony, the false witnesses are exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the accused was already sentenced to pay when the first witnesses testified, they do not pay even after being proven זוממין.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהודה calls it a conspiracy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה's words, "this is a conspiracy," to begin discussing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says, "This is a conspiracy," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. It quotes רבי יהודה's line from the משנה to set up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, one pair of witnesses proved many groups of witnesses false. רבי יהודה sees this as a planned conspiracy and limits the punishment. Here the גמרא only quotes his opening words. The discussion continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: "Etc.": the rest of the quote from the משנה continues

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִיסְטָטִית הִיא זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of רבא's rules and goes back to the משנה to discuss רבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quoting the משנה: רבי יהודה calls the repeated הזמה by one pair of witnesses an איסטטית, a conspiracy.
